prompt:
sqlglot only understands some forms of Oracle's alternative quoting (q'[...]'). Oracle allows any delimiter after q': the brackets [ ] { } ( ) < > close with their partner, any other character closes with itself, the q may be upper or lower case, and the national form nq'...' (any case) gives an N'...' literal. Quotes and newlines inside the literal must be kept, the literal must round-trip, and text inside such literals must not be mistaken for SQL tokens.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("SELECT q']it's]' FROM dual", read="oracle").sql("oracle")
# currently: TokenError: Error tokenizing 'SELECT q']it's]' FROM dua'
# expected:  SELECT 'it''s' FROM dual

parse_one("SELECT Q'Ait'sA' FROM dual", read="oracle").sql("oracle")
# currently: TokenError: Error tokenizing 'SELECT Q'Ait'sA' FROM dua'
# expected:  SELECT 'it''s' FROM dual

parse_one("SELECT nq'[it's]' FROM dual", read="oracle").sql("oracle")
# currently: TokenError: Error tokenizing 'SELECT nq'[it's]' FROM dua'
# expected:  SELECT N'it''s' FROM dual
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
